text: A 12,000-worker survey found blood pressure fell 11 points, but only among those who cut salt.
Coffee gave sleep-deprived students a 2 percent memory boost on one word-list test.
Working from home raised productivity in three startups' software teams, but the gains vanished after six months.
The new bridge saved bus passengers about twenty minutes on average, compared with a year of roadworks.
Vitamin D may prevent colds, but that was seen only in under-fives in one supplement-funded winter trial.
A reading app helped English-learning children, but the gains faded by the next school year.
A pesticide study found bumblebee colonies produced a quarter fewer queens in one season.
A four-day week in Icelandic public offices reduced burnout, with pay unchanged and no change in sick days.
